Threat / vulnerability: Supervised model only recognises attack patterns present in training data
Evidence: Recall on 17 unseen attack types 39.5% vs 78.2% on known types (results/per_category_recall.csv)
Treatment actions: Add anomaly layer (Isolation Forest trained on normal traffic only) - measured unseen recall 65.9%; keep signature IDS for known attacks; subscribe to threat intelligence and add new attack samples each quarter

Risk: Credential and default-account attacks invisible to flow-based IDS
Threat / vulnerability: Flow features cannot see password guessing or use of default SNMP/FTP credentials
Evidence: 0% detection for T1110.001 (1,562 records) and 23% for T1078.001 (results/mitre_by_technique.csv)
Treatment actions: Enforce MFA and account lockout; SIEM alert on >10 failed logins in 5 min; remove default SNMP community strings and anonymous FTP; quarterly access review

Risk: Exploits, privilege escalation and tunnelling missed
Threat / vulnerability: Attack payloads look like normal sessions at flow level
Treatment actions: EDR on all servers; monthly patch cycle with critical patches in 7 days; WAF on public apps; egress filtering through proxy

Threat / vulnerability: Go-live decision based on cross-validation or vendor numbers
Evidence: Cross-validation F1 99.9% vs 79.2% on realistic test set - 20-point gap (results/cv_binary.csv vs metrics_binary.csv)
Treatment actions: Acceptance test on the organisation's own labelled traffic before go-live; documented acceptance criteria (recall, FPR); model card reviewed by risk committee

Risk: Model drift degrades detection over time
Threat / vulnerability: Traffic mix and attacker behaviour change after training
Evidence: 5 features with moderate PSI shift in normal traffic (dst_host_diff_srv_rate 0.117) between training and test data (results/guardrails_drift_psi.csv)
Treatment actions: Monthly PSI report; retrain trigger when any feature PSI > 0.25 or recall on validation set drops > 5 points; quarterly scheduled retraining under change management

Threat / vulnerability: Attackers pad traffic so it scores as normal
Evidence: Padding bytes/duration made 16-17% of detected attacks evade (results/guardrails_evasion.csv)
Treatment actions: Adversarial training with padded samples; rely more on rate-based features; hybrid with anomaly layer and signatures; annual red-team test of the model

Evidence: FPR 2.8% at threshold 0.5; 9.2% at threshold 0.05 (results/guardrails_threshold.csv). At 100,000 normal connections/day: ~2,800 false alerts
Treatment actions: Three-band decision policy (auto-alert >=0.7, analyst review 0.2-0.7, allow <0.2) - only 6.4% of events go to analysts; alert enrichment with asset and user context; monthly threshold review

Risk: Personal data in network logs and training sets
Threat / vulnerability: IP addresses, usernames and session data are personal data
Evidence: DPDP Act 2023 (breach report to Data Protection Board within 72 h); CERT-In requires 180-day log retention
Treatment actions: Pseudonymise IPs/usernames in training data; role-based access to feature store; retention 180 days for logs then deletion; record processing purpose; include in DPIA

Threat / vulnerability: Unauthorised change to labelled training data
Evidence: Not tested in this project - identified in threat model (T2)
Treatment actions: SHA-256 hashes and version control for datasets; write access limited to 2 named people; label changes peer-reviewed

Threat / vulnerability: No separation between model development and deployment
Treatment actions: All model releases through change management with rollback plan; separate dev/prod; deployment only by CI pipeline

Risk: Detection decisions cannot be explained in audits or investigations
Threat / vulnerability: Ensemble/neural network decisions are not transparent
Evidence: Feature importance available for Random Forest only (results/feature_importance.csv)
Treatment actions: Attach top contributing features to each alert; maintain model card; keep scored events with model version for 180 days

Threat / vulnerability: Detection-to-report process too slow for CERT-In 6 h / DPDP 72 h
Evidence: CERT-In Directions 2022; DPDP Rules 2025 (breach reporting applies from May 2027)
Treatment actions: Incident playbook with CERT-In and DPDP steps; NTP time sync on all log sources; quarterly tabletop exercise

Risk: IDS becomes a single point of failure under load
Evidence: Measured 117k-134k records/s for tree models, SVM 25k/s (results/metrics_binary.csv); depends on hardware, GitHub runners scored 180k-277k/s
Treatment actions: Load test at 3x peak; horizontal scaling; fail-safe to signature IDS if ML service is down; capacity monitoring

Threat / vulnerability: Only one person understands the model
Treatment actions: Runbooks for retraining and threshold changes; train 2 SOC analysts on model behaviour; documented model card
